title: Build a passage map
summary: Map the topic, purpose of each paragraph and overall development before answering detailed comprehension questions.

sections.title: Name the job of a paragraph
content: A paragraph does more than contain facts. It may introduce a problem, explain a method, present evidence, contrast ideas or show a result.
Read one short paragraph and summarise its job in no more than six words. This trains you to see structure without copying sentences.

sections.title: Use topic, job and link
content: Topic: identify who or what the whole passage is mainly about.
Job: label each paragraph with a short verb phrase such as introduces the problem, explains the plan or reports the outcome.
Link: notice how the paragraph connects to the previous one through chronology, cause and effect, contrast, example or conclusion.
Keep the map brief. Detailed notes consume time and can hide the passage's main development.

sections.title: Follow a problem-to-impact structure
content: Suppose paragraph 1 describes a flooded courtyard, paragraph 2 explains a student investigation, paragraph 3 reports the first test and paragraph 4 lists later benefits.
The map is problem → investigation and proposal → evidence → wider impact. This structure helps distinguish the central idea from supporting details.
A reference phrase such as “this result” must point to an earlier event in the map, while a synonym answer must preserve the exact meaning and word role in its sentence.

sections.title: Build the map in one minute
content: Read the title and first sentence of every paragraph, then read the complete passage. Write one short job label beside each paragraph.
Check whether your labels form a logical sequence. Revise any label that merely repeats a detail instead of describing the paragraph's purpose.

sections.title: Answer from bounded evidence
content: Use the paragraph navigator to return to the exact location named in a question. Answer only from the passage, even when you know more about the topic.
For short-text questions, copy only the requested word or state the referent precisely. For multiple-response questions, verify every selected statement separately.

sections.title: Find where the reading process failed
content: Missed clue: the relevant sentence or paragraph was not located.
Option trap: a choice repeated passage words but changed their relationship.
Tone mismatch: a choice was stronger, weaker or more emotional than the passage.
Unknown meaning: a key word or option prevented an accurate interpretation. Record one cause before retrying.

sections.title: A second life for the school courtyard
content: Map and answer one original four-paragraph passage. All responses are marked together so feedback from an early question cannot reveal a later answer.
